title: focus-week-retreat-facilitator-cheat-sheet-v0-1
content:
Purpose: Lightweight facilitator reference for a 3-day focus-week retreat that aligns exec priorities, drafts Q2 OKRs, and produces a tight all-hands narrative. This is intentionally deckless — use short artifacts, whiteboarding, and a single shared notes doc. Treat as scratch-first; capture decisions and owners in the decision log section at bottom.

High-level goals:
- Get executive alignment on top 3 company priorities for the next 90 days (one technology, one go-to-market, one platform/ops).
- Produce a first-pass set of OKR candidates with clear owners and success metrics (numerical where possible).
- Prepare an all-hands 15-minute narrative + 10-min AMA that reflects decisions and early asks.
- Leave with a 30/60/90-day roll-forward and 10 prioritized action items with owners.

Prework (send 5 working days before):
- Short survey to all execs: top risks, top opportunities (3 bullets each). Deadline: 72h before start.
- Collate product telemetry snapshot: latency percentiles, cost per 1M tokens, infra utilization. (SRE).
- One-pager per major initiative (max 1 page). Use template: outcome, metric, current status, required asks.
- All-hands draft outline (see "All-hands narrative" below) — Communications to own final slide.

Day 0 (prep):
- Room: big whiteboard, sticky notes, projector; remote: low-latency breakout rooms, shared Miro.
- Facilitator checklist: sticky labels for priority voting, printed role cards (timekeeper, scribe, escalation owner).

Day 1 — Diagnose & Surface (4 hours)
- 09:00–09:20: Kickoff & context (CEO) — set the working contract: speed over perfection; decisions today are directional.
- 09:20–10:30: Data sprint — four short signals: latency/cost, reliability incidents, sales pipeline health, customer escalations. 5 min per signal + 10 min Qs.
- 10:30–11:30: Problem framing: round-robin of top risks/opps from exec survey. Use 3x5 sticky notes (problem/opportunity/naive-metric).
- 11:30–12:00: Dot-vote to pick top 6 themes for deeper work.
- 13:00–16:00: Breakout deep dives (choice of 3 themes per room). Outcome: crisp problem statement, 1 hypothesis, 1 success metric, 3 starting projects.

Facilitator tips (Day 1):
- Keep rooms focused: every breakout must output a 1-paragraph problem statement and 3 line-item projects.
- Timebox relentlessly; use visible countdowns for synth.
- Encourage counterfactuals: what would failure look like? what is the simplest way to know we are wrong?

Day 2 — Decide & Draft OKRs (5 hours)
- 09:00–09:15: Quick warm-up and review of Day 1 outputs (scribe reads).
- 09:15–10:45: Prioritization matrix exercise: impact (customer reach / revenue / platform stability) vs effort (E weeks). Each theme gets a point estimate and a confidence band.
- 10:45–12:30: OKR drafting session in pairs (owner + subject-matter exec): draft 2–3 objectives with 2–4 key results each. Use numeric KRs where possible (latency p95 ms, tokens per $, NPS delta, deploys/week).
- 13:30–15:00: OKR readout + rapid challenge (5 min readout, 5 min cross-exec critique). Capture suggested edits inline.
- 15:00–16:00: Consolidate into a single candidate OKR list and rank top 6 KRs to instrument first.

Decision rules (to enforce when debates stall):
- If we can’t agree on wording, convert to a temporary, named hypothesis owned by someone with 30-day check-in.
- For conflicting resource asks, prefer the option with measurable customer-facing outcome.
- If two initiatives are equally critical, schedule a razor test (small timebox POC) and re-evaluate in 21 days.

Day 3 — Operationalize & Communicate (3.5 hours)
- 09:00–10:00: 30/60/90 plan — for each top objective assign: lead, 30-day milestone, 60-day milestone, key blockers, runbook owner.
- 10:00–11:00: All-hands narrative rehearsal (CEO + comms): 15-min narrative, 10-min AMA structure, 3 live demo/spotlight slots (product/customer/sre).
- 11:00–12:30: Comms and escalation plan: how we publish OKRs, cadence for updates, who owns retros and exceptions.

All-hands narrative (15-min outline):
- 2 min: Orientation — where the company is today (one data slide: latency/cost or revenue trend).
- 4 min: The 3 priorities for next 90 days (1 slide each: goal, why, measurable sign of success).
- 4 min: What this means for engineers/product/CS (concrete asks).
- 3 min: Early wins & signals we’ll watch.
- 2 min: Logistics: how to follow, where to see the OKRs, how to submit questions.

Facilitator heuristics for the narrative:
- Keep it short. Replace adjectives with metrics. For engineers: say exactly what will change in their day-to-day (e.g., "reduce blocking incidents by 30%; on-call shifts reduced to X").
- Limit asks to no more than 3 cross-org actions.

Risk & fallback playbook:
- If an OKR requires >50% of Dedicated capacity for two months, create an emergency review and a fallback model variant (re-route traffic, autoscale config, or temporary quota).
- If a major customer demands a SLA that conflicts with cost targets, escalate to CFO + SRE for a trade-off desk within 48h.

Capture and artifacts (how we record things):
- Single source of truth: this Drive doc becomes the working notes. Always append date/time and initials when editing key sections.
- Decision log: use table at bottom (Date | Decision | Owner | Rationale | Follow-up).
- Action tracker: create a short sheet with columns: action, owner, due, status, blockers, related KR. Link in linked_artifacts.

Post-retreat ops (first 14 days):
- Day +2: Publish candidate OKRs and 30/60/90 plan to all staff. Comms owner: Sana Iqbal.
- Day +7: Instrument the top 6 KRs in the dashboard. Owner: Eng-Platform analytics.
- Day +14: First 30-day pulse and retro (what we learned about the planning process).

Decision log (starter rows):
- 2026-02-18 | Prioritize: Reduce inference-per-token cost as company priority | Owner: Diego Alvarez | Rationale: Unit economics stress in telemetry, affects sales motion | Follow-up: Confirm candidate quant target by 02-25
- 2026-02-19 | All-hands format: 15min narrative + 10min AMA | Owner: CEO | Rationale: Shorter tempo for better engagement | Follow-up: Comms to finalize by 02-22

Open questions / to resolve this week:
- What is a realistic % reduction in p95 latency achievable without increasing infra costs? (SRE to model: option sets + rough $ delta).
- Can finance provide a 3-month runway impact assessment if we commit to the Dedicated capacity safety buffer? (Finance).
- Which customer-facing metric does Sales want prioritized for Q2 (MRR expansion vs retention signals)?

Notes to facilitator (voice):
- Be candid and surface trade-offs — people expect nuance.
- Default to provisional language: label anything not fully agreed as "hypothesis: owner — review date".
- When tension arises, move to a tiny experiment rather than multi-month commitments.

Appendix: Short OKR drafting template (copy into a shared doc for each pair)
- Objective (1 line): 
- Why it matters (1 line): 
- KR1 (numeric): baseline -> target -> owner
- KR2 (numeric or binary with measurement): baseline -> target -> owner
- KR3 (optional supporting KR)
- What would show failure?
- First 30-day milestone

End: capture next update cadence (biweekly exec check-ins, monthly all-staff pulse), then close with a short facilitator retrospective prompt: "what slowed us? what accelerated us? what should change next planning cycle?"

-- notes to self: keep all artifacts under /shared_drives/company/misc/focus-week-2026; export final OKRs to Confluence and create a lightweight dashboard card for top 6 KRs.
